style: Photorealistic cinematic still, natural light, shallow depth of field where stated, muted documentary colour grade, 16:9. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no modern objects unless stated.

shots.prompt: Extreme close-up of a single carbonised Herculaneum papyrus scroll lying on a dark wooden table under one warm lamp in a dark room: a black, cracked, slightly crushed cylinder about 7 cm across and 15 cm long, its surface blistered and flaking like burnt charcoal, faint fine layers visible at one broken end. Dark background, single pool of light.

Same black carbonised scroll from the reference, now resting in the palm of an adult's cupped bare hand above the dark table, the hand holding it very gently; small black flakes have broken off onto the palm. Same warm single lamp, dark background, macro photograph.

1750s excavation tunnel cut through grey-brown volcanic rock near Naples, lit by smoky pitch torches: two or three workmen in rough linen shirts, breeches and caps, seen from behind and in shadow so no faces are visible, kneel by a heap of dozens of black charred cylinders they have dug out, one lump being tossed toward a glowing brazier. Smoke, dust, warm torchlight.

Same black carbonised scroll from the reference, seen end-on in macro: the broken end shows tightly rolled, paper-thin spiral layers of blackened papyrus like the rings of a tree, revealing that it is a rolled book, not wood. Warm side light, dark background.

Mount Vesuvius erupting at night in 79 AD seen from across the Bay of Naples: a towering ash column narrow at the crater widening into an umbrella cloud, lightning in the cloud, a dull orange glow at the summit, the dark sea in front reflecting it. No lava rivers, no people, no modern buildings.

An 18th-century scholar's workbench lit by a window: a black carbonised scroll cut open and crumbling into many small black flakes and fragments on a sheet of paper, a small knife and brush beside them, the pieces broken and scattered. No people visible, documentary still life.

Modern scientific lab in near darkness: a small black carbonised scroll mounted upright in a clear holder on a rotating stage inside an X-ray scanner, a thin bright beam line crossing it, a computer monitor in the background showing a grey 3D spiral of the scroll's layers. Cool blue light. No people, no readable text on the screen.
Same black carbonised scroll from the reference on the dark table under the single warm lamp, seen a little wider, the room dark around it, quiet and mysterious.

cards.text: THE LIBRARY WE DESTROYED TRYING TO READ
